commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to heave the weight up
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears at the top
Pressing the weights out in front instead of overhead
cues: Ribs down, glutes squeezed — no lean-back
Press up and slightly in, biceps finishing by your ears
Lower with control to the starting position every rep
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing each other or slightly forward. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the weights overhead until your arms are fully extended, biceps finishing roughly by your ears. Do not lean back.
Pause briefly at the top without shrugging your shoulders.
Lower the weights back to shoulder height with control. That is one rep.
longevityNotes: Overhead strength is independence: putting luggage in the bin, reaching the top shelf, catching yourself in a fall. The standing press builds it while forcing the core and glutes to stabilize — a full-body investment from one movement. Keep the loads moderate and the reps clean; cranky shoulders come from grinding heavy singles, not from patient sub-maximal volume.
name: Overhead Press

progression.loadingGuidance: Add the smallest available increment when you can complete 3 sets of 10 with no back arch at RPE 7 or less.

safetyNotes: If you have shoulder impingement, keep the reps pain-free and stop well short of lockout if the top position pinches. Never press behind the neck.
